reason: R2 is part of the resistive bridge tying VOUT1/VOUT2 to the common node net04; removing it preserves the core amplification path (M3/M5 with PMOS loads M7/M6) but weakens the output common-mode coupling. Caveat: net04 may become less well-defined and the two outputs can become less balanced unless the remaining network still biases net04 adequately.

R3 plays the symmetric role to R2 for VOUT2; removing it keeps the active devices functioning while reducing the resistive averaging/coupling into net04. Caveat: removing only one of R2/R3 introduces asymmetry; if you remove one, typically remove the other or ensure net04 is defined elsewhere.

M1 is a diode-connected NMOS clamp/pulldown on VOUT1 set by net04; if the output does not require an explicit sink/clamp path (e.g., load provides it), the PMOS load and input device can still produce an output voltage. Caveat: VOUT1 may float high or lose bias stability/settling and swing control, especially if net04 also becomes weakly defined when R2/R3 are removed.
impact_estimate: Medium (affects output bias and swing stability on VOUT1)
